citation.source: Refined sunflower oil's commonly-cited smoke point is ~227-232°C (440-450°F) — notably higher than oil.json's olive oil (200°C), the real reason it's the more common choice for higher-heat/deep-frying in practice, including in Spain (often cheaper and more heat-tolerant than olive oil for this specific use, even though olive oil remains the default for lower-heat cooking and flavor). densityKgPerM3/specificHeatJPerKgK reuse oil.json's own values/reasoning (same order-of-magnitude triglyceride oil, no independently-sourced sunflower-specific figure found for either this session) — see oil.json's own citation for the 'roughly half of water's specific heat' heuristic this also relies on.
citation.note: Added 2026-08-14, directly answering 'what changes if I fry with a different oil' — the concrete second entity proving requiredIngredientCapabilities' isFryingMedium check was already substitutable (unlike requiredTools' pre-2026-08-14 exact-id problem, this mechanism never needed a fix, only a second real entity to prove it).

metadata.notes: Second real frying-medium entity, added specifically to prove data/actions/fry.json's requiredIngredientCapabilities: ['isFryingMedium'] check is genuinely substitutable, not implicitly hardcoded to oil.json (olive oil) the way requiredTools was for pot/pan before the 2026-08-14 requiredToolCapabilities fix. See scripts/fry-with-different-fats.ts for FRY actually executing with this entity as the ingredient, and for the real consequence of its HIGHER smoke point vs. olive oil: more thermal headroom at FRY's upper oilTempC range (191°C, crispy_french_fries.json's finishing fry) than olive oil's own 200°C ceiling leaves.
